4. The first harmonic for a pipe that is closed at one end, such as a didgeridoo, will have one pressure
node (N) and one pressure antinode (A), as shown in the diagram.
How many pressure nodes must there be for the third harmonic?
Pipes that are closed at one end must have a pressure antinode at the closed end and a pressure node at the open end.
Given that the wavelength of the first harmonic is four times the length of the pipe, a second harmonic cannot form;
it would be twice the length of the pipe, which would result in a pressure antinode at the open end. The third
harmonic has a wavelength that is 4/3 times longer than the length of the pipe, resulting in two pressure nodes as,
